Muskoka Sauna Co

Project Brief
Coastline Films partnered with Muskoka Sauna Co. on an ongoing monthly retainer, producing over 20 individual shoots as part of a long-term creative growth program. What began as a single campaign evolved into a full creative partnership, with Coastline Films embedded in how the brand is built rather than hired shoot to shoot. The work spans cinematic product, lifestyle, and brand content designed to grow Muskoka Sauna Co.'s audience and consistently move product, shot across seasons and tailored to their customer at every step. Content is created for use across social media, digital advertising, and ongoing brand marketing, with a steady cadence of new material keeping the brand active and top of mind year-round.

Here is what video production actually costs in Ontario in 2026, what drives the price up or down, and how to tell whether you should be buying a one-off shoot or a monthly content retainer. All numbers are in CAD.</p><h2>How much does video production cost in Ontario? The short answer</h2><p>For professional work from an established production company in Toronto, Muskoka or anywhere else in Ontario, these are realistic ranges:</p><ul><li><strong>Social content shoot:</strong> $1,500 to $5,000</li><li><strong>Brand film (60 to 120 seconds):</strong> $8,000 to $35,000</li><li><strong>Multi-asset campaign:</strong> $20,000 to $75,000</li><li><strong>National broadcast commercial:</strong> $75,000 to $250,000+</li><li><strong>Monthly content retainer:</strong> $1,800 to $10,000+ per month</li></ul><p>If a quote lands far below these ranges, someone is cutting a corner: no pre-production, one person doing everything, no colour grade, stock music, or no usage rights spelled out. If it lands far above, you are usually paying for broadcast-level crew, talent, travel, or an agency markup on top of the production company.</p><p>The range is wide because "a video" is not one product. The rest of this guide breaks down exactly where the money goes.</p><h2>What actually drives the cost of a video</h2><p>Every quote is built from the same handful of levers. Once you understand them, you can read any proposal and know whether it is fair.</p><h3>1. Pre-production: the part you do not see</h3><p>Concept, script or story outline, shot list, location scouting, scheduling, talent casting and permits. On a small social shoot this might be a few hours. On a commercial it can be two to four weeks of work. Expect pre-production to be roughly 10 to 20 percent of the budget.</p><p>This is the line item cheap quotes skip, and it is the one that decides whether the final video actually sells anything. A shoot without a plan is just expensive footage.</p><h3>2. Shoot days and crew size</h3><p>This is the biggest single driver. A lean crew of one or two (director/shooter plus an assistant or drone operator) for a day typically runs $2,500 to $6,000. Add a dedicated director of photography, gaffer, sound, producer and hair and makeup, and a single day can move to $10,000 to $25,000 before talent and locations.</p><p>More days, more people, more cost. The trick is matching crew size to what the content actually needs. A lifestyle shoot for Instagram does not need a 15-person crew. A national broadcast spot does.</p><h3>3. Gear: cinema cameras, lenses, drones and lighting</h3><p>Cinema camera packages, quality lenses, drones, gimbals and lighting are usually built into a day rate or listed separately. On water, in the backcountry or in winter, add specialty gear like boat mounts or extra batteries and weather protection. This is where premium work separates itself visually.</p><h3>4. Locations, travel and logistics</h3><p>Shooting at your own resort, showroom or job site is the cheapest option. Renting a cottage, a boat or a studio adds cost. So does travel: a Toronto crew driving to Muskoka, or a Muskoka crew flying to the west coast, means mileage, accommodation and per diems.</p><p>Coastline is based in Squamish, BC, with regular shoots across Ontario, from cottage country to the GTA. We also regularly travel for work, Canada-wide and beyond.</p><h3>5. Talent</h3><p>Using your own staff or customers is free (and often more authentic). Professional actors and models cost anywhere from a few hundred dollars per day for non-union lifestyle talent to significantly more for union performers on a broadcast spot, plus buyout fees based on where and how long the ad runs.</p><h3>6. Post-production</h3><p>Editing, colour grading, sound design and mixing, licensed music, motion graphics and revisions. A good rule: post-production takes as long as, or longer than, the shoot. Cutting one hero video plus ten social versions in vertical and horizontal formats is real work, and it should be priced like it.</p><h3>7. Usage rights and deliverables</h3><p>How many versions do you need, in what formats, and where will they run? Organic social is the simplest. Paid ads, TV broadcast and out-of-home add music licensing and talent usage costs. Always make sure your quote spells out what you own and where you can use it.</p><h2>Sample budgets: what different businesses typically spend</h2><p>Here is how those levers come together for the kinds of businesses we work with across Ontario.</p><h3>A resort or hotel launching a new season</h3><p>Two shoot days on property, a lean-to-mid crew, drone, lifestyle talent, one 60 to 90 second hero film and 10 to 15 short social cuts. Typical range: <strong>$12,000 to $30,000</strong>. Our work with <a href="https://www.coastlinefilms.ca/projects/blackrockoceanfront">Black Rock Resort</a> is an example of this kind of cinematic, booking-focused content.</p><h3>A custom home builder showing off finished builds</h3><p>One to two days capturing completed homes in their setting, plus process footage on active sites. Clean, design-driven cinematography and photography cut for Instagram and ads. Typical range: <strong>$5,000 to $15,000</strong> per campaign. See how we approached this with <a href="https://www.coastlinefilms.ca/projects/hldmuskoka">HLD Muskoka</a>.</p><h3>A marine dealer or premium consumer brand</h3><p>Product and lifestyle shooting, often on the water, with drone and detail shots across multiple models or products. Typical range: <strong>$10,000 to $40,000</strong> depending on the number of products and locations. Our <a href="https://www.coastlinefilms.ca/projects/pridemarina">Pride Marina</a> campaign is a good reference point.</p><h3>A national brand running a broadcast campaign</h3><p>Full crew, casting, multiple locations across the country, a hero broadcast spot and months of social rollout. Typical range: <strong>$75,000 and up</strong>. (2026 Guide)" class="post-section-img w-dyn-bind-empty"/><p class="post-section-caption w-dyn-bind-empty"></p></div><div class="post-rich-text w-richtext"><h2>One-off shoot vs monthly retainer: which one is cheaper?</h2><p>This is the question that matters most, and the answer surprises people.</p><p>A one-off shoot is the right call when you have a single, clear moment: a launch, a new property, a broadcast campaign, a brand film you will use for years. You pay once, you get a polished asset, and you are done.</p><p>The problem is that most businesses do not have a "one video" problem. They have a "we need to show up every week and we have nothing to post" problem. One-off shoots solve that for about six weeks. Then the content runs dry, the feed goes quiet, and you are back to quoting another shoot from scratch. Every time you restart, you pay again for pre-production, onboarding and a crew that has to learn your brand all over again.</p><p>A monthly content retainer flips that. You get a set number of shoot days and deliverables every month, the same team every time, and a production partner that already knows your product, your customer and your look. Pre-production gets faster, every shoot builds on the last one, and the cost per finished piece of content drops hard.</p><p>At Coastline Films, retainers start from <strong>$1,800 per month CAD</strong>. That is less than many companies charge for a single shoot day, spread into a consistent content engine instead of a one-time spike.</p><h3>What a retainer looks like in practice</h3><p>Our longest-running example is <a href="https://www.coastlinefilms.ca/projects/msco">Muskoka Sauna Co.</a> What started as a single campaign turned into an ongoing monthly retainer: more than 20 individual shoots across two seasons, covering cinematic product, lifestyle and brand content. Over that time the brand built an audience of 70,000 followers, with a steady cadence of new content that keeps them top of mind year-round and keeps product moving.</p><p>That result does not come from one great video. It comes from showing up with great content every single month.</p><h2>How to get an accurate video production quote</h2><p>The tighter you can describe what you need, the tighter the quote. Walk in with answers to these: who are you selling to, where will the content run, how many finished pieces do you need, do you have talent and locations or do we source them, and what is the deadline. Any production company that cannot sharpen those with you in a 15-minute call is not the right partner.</p><h2>Red flags when comparing quotes</h2><p>Watch out for a quote with no breakdown of pre-production, shoot and post, a day rate without a crew list, no mention of colour grade or sound mix, no licensed music budget, vague deliverables ("a few social videos"), and no usage rights spelled out. If you cannot see where the money goes, you cannot judge whether it is fair.</p><p>The fastest way to judge a production company is to watch their work. Browse <a href="https://www.coastlinefilms.ca/work">our portfolio</a> and ask yourself one question: does this look like the brand you want to be?</p><h2>Frequently asked questions</h2><h3>How much does a 1 minute video cost in Ontario?</h3><p>A professionally produced 60 second video typically costs $3,000 to $15,000 CAD. A simple social piece with a lean crew sits at the low end. A scripted brand video with talent, multiple locations and a full colour grade and sound mix sits at the high end. Length matters far less than shoot days, crew and post-production.</p><h3>What is the day rate for a videographer in Toronto or Muskoka?</h3><p>A solo professional videographer typically charges $1,000 to $2,500 per day in Ontario. A small production crew with a director, camera operator and gear package usually runs $2,500 to $6,000 per day. Editing is generally billed separately.</p><h3>Is a monthly video retainer worth it for a small business?</h3><p>If you post on social or run ads, usually yes. A retainer lowers your cost per piece of content, removes the restart cost of new shoots, and gives you a consistent presence that one-off shoots cannot. Coastline Films retainers start from $1,800 per month CAD.</p><h3>How long does a video production take?</h3><p>A simple social shoot can be turned around in one to two weeks. A brand film usually takes four to eight weeks from kickoff to final delivery. (function () {
  var EASE = 0.09;

  function distToRect(mx, my, r) {
    var dx = Math.max(r.left - mx, 0, mx - r.right);
    var dy = Math.max(r.top  - my, 0, my - r.bottom);
    return Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
  }

  function makeTilt(el, max, prox, persp) {
    var rotX=0, rotY=0, rotXT=0, rotYT=0, raf=null;

    function tick() {
      rotX = lerp(rotX, rotXT, EASE);
      rotY = lerp(rotY, rotYT, EASE);
      el.style.transform =
        'perspective(' + persp + 'px) ' +
        'rotateX(' + rotX.toFixed(3) + 'deg) ' +
        'rotateY(' + rotY.toFixed(3) + 'deg)';
      var done = Math.abs(rotX - rotXT) < 0.005 && Math.abs(rotY - rotYT) < 0.005;
      if (done) {
        raf = null;
        if (rotXT === 0 && rotYT === 0) el.style.transform = '';
      } else {
        raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      }
    }
    function go() { if (!raf) raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }

    /* attach to both element AND document so proximity zone works */
    function onMove(e) {
      var r    = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      var dist = distToRect(e.clientX, e.clientY, r);
      if (dist <= prox) {
        var cx = r.left + r.width  / 2;
        var cy = r.top  + r.height / 2;
        var dx = (e.clientX - cx) / (r.width  / 2 + prox);
        var dy = (e.clientY - cy) / (r.height / 2 + prox);
        var s  = 1 - dist / prox;
        rotYT =  dx * max * s;
        rotXT = -dy * max * s;
      } else {
        rotXT = 0; rotYT = 0;
      }
      go();
    }

    document.addEventListener('mousemove', onMove, { passive: true });
  }

    /* guard: skip already-initialised elements */
    document.querySelectorAll('[data-f-tilt]:not([data-f-ready])').forEach(function (el) {
